title: Lena Horne as Leona, Will Mastin, not begging, the Three Palms
summary: Albertson mentions a picture of young Lena conducting Noble Sissle's band; Hunter wants to contact Will Mastin and Sammy's father and thinks secretaries block her letters. The dancers the Three Palms and drummer Herbie Cowan's band were with her on the European theater tour.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Do you remember her when she was with Noble Sissle?
Who, Lena?
Lena Horne.
I remember little Lena, bless her little old pretty heart.
Leona Horne or something like that.
Leona?
I saw a picture in the --
I don't know Leona Horne.

-- Amsterdam News from the late '30s, there's a picture of her and she's got a baton in her hand, and it says, "Pretty Miss Leona Horne, fresh out of high school, conducts the Noble Sissle Orchestra."
Oh, bless her little heart. Well, I didn't know that.
"We understand she's a chirper, too."

I didn't know that. That was before me. I don't know that. Not before my time, but I don't know about that. But I want to make it plain. So anytime any of the performers get a letter from me, it's just that I'm inquiring about them because I would like to hear from them. And Will Mastin, who is the uncle of Sammy, the Will Mastin Trio?
Yes.
I would like very much to contact him and Sammy's father, because I used to go and sit in their dressing room every day while I was trying to find work, several times, you know.
Is his father still alive?
Yes.
He is?

Uh-huh. Yes. I used to go and sit in their dressing room and talk with them, and Sammy ran out on the stage when he was nothing but a kid, in Boston. We were on the same program. So anytime I write them, if they want to answer, all right, but if they don't, all right. But I want them to know I'm not begging.
Yeah.
Because I don't need anything.
Of course he may not even know that you ever wrote to him.
Well see, the thing of it is, some of them have these little fresh, smart secretaries, you know.
Yeah.

And they see Alberta, they see it's a woman, and they think it's somebody trying to get friendly with him or something, and don't answer. But I'm old enough to be his great grandmother, so they can answer, you know. Some of them have -- chances are Billy Eckstine didn't get that letter.
Yeah.
Because I sent it to Westbury, and there's no way in the world for them to say unknown, because he was working there.
That's right.
See, so how is he unknown? I was simply asking for his record.
Well, I'm going to get you the record.
Oh, I'd give anything in the world to get that record.
But have we left anything out?
Yes.
What?
Now, did you get in there about the Three Palms? They were with me.
Now, this was a group you were on a USO tour with.
Yes, uh-huh.
They were dancers.
Yeah. They had dancers. Well, the band with me was Herbie Cowan. Herbie Cowan was the drummer but it was his band. And we did -- oh, we did so well. That was on the ETO, the ETO group.
